comparison: Both strongly support the whole-cell mechanosensitive response data (C6, C7, C40-C52). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree this is technically impressive and well-controlled. Peer review also includes C131-C132 (main conclusions about NaChBac mechanosensitivity and similarity to NaV1.5) in this evaluation.

Both support the single-channel data showing pressure-induced increases in PO (C8, C53, C57, C61-C70). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the technical achievement and voltage-dependent mechanosensitive response are convincing. Peer review additionally includes C63-C64 and C138 in their evaluation.

OpenEval supports reversibility claims (C72-C77) based on NaChBac data, while peer reviewers express uncertainty, initially requesting additional reversibility data for NaV1.5 (Essential revision #3), suggesting incomplete evidence in the original submission.

Both address MSA model and its rejection (C85-C93). OpenEval supports the model construction and experimental contradiction. Peer review supports the broader mechanistic conclusion distinguishing MSO from MSA (also including C9-C10, C94-C99, C105, C107-C108, C141-C143), treating this as a key conceptual advance.

OpenEval supports MSO model validation and dwell time analysis (C94-C108). Peer review supports the core MSO mechanism (C94-C99, C105, C107-C108) as a conceptual advance, with substantial overlap in claims about the mechanosensitive step having little voltage sensitivity.

OpenEval supports dwell time analysis showing pressure effects on opening rates (C101-C104, C106). Peer reviewers express uncertainty, with Reviewer #1 challenging the closed lifetime shift claim and requesting stronger evidence or removal of the claim.

OpenEval supports mutagenesis data (C115-C123), particularly I228G results showing pore involvement. Peer reviewers express significant uncertainty about I228G interpretation, noting 'multiple interpretations are plausible' and that 'the logic remains unclear,' suggesting the mechanism is not definitively established.

OpenEval supports inferences about mechanosensitivity affecting activation/opening rather than inactivation (C78-C84, C136-C137). Peer review supports the core mechanistic conclusion (C13, C78-C80, C136-C137, C139-C140, C144-C145, C170-C171) as a conceptual advance, affirming that Nav channels respond to pressure by affecting a conformational change with little voltage dependence.

OpenEval supports main conclusions about pore-dependent mechanosensitivity (C131-C134, C170-C171). Peer review supports the core mechanistic finding (C13, C78-C80, C136-C137, C170-C171) but requested softening of speculation about structural details.

OpenEval supports main conclusions (C131-C134, C170-C171). Peer review includes C131-C132 (demonstration of NaChBac mechanosensitivity and similarity to NaV1.5) in their evaluation of whole-cell data, treating these as well-established.

OpenEval expresses uncertainty about extrapolation to eukaryotic channels (C13-C14, C146, C150), noting lack of direct experimental validation. Peer reviewers also express uncertainty (C14, C130, C133, C146, C150), requesting that evolutionary claims and extrapolations be 'substantially softened.'

OpenEval supports structural analysis and force-from-lipid model integration (C109, C111-C114). Peer reviewers express uncertainty about structural interpretations and force-from-lipid mechanism (C109, C111-C112, C114, C147-C160), requesting that speculation about structural changes be more strongly supported or softened.

OpenEval supports theoretical framework for mechanotransduction and force-from-lipid model (C151-C160, C168). Peer reviewers express uncertainty about these structural and mechanistic interpretations (C109, C111-C112, C114, C147-C160), requesting stronger support or substantial softening of speculation.

OpenEval expresses uncertainty about physiological and therapeutic implications (C161-C169, C172), noting they are speculative extrapolations. Peer reviewers also express uncertainty (C161-C169, C172), explicitly requesting that claims about physiological relevance be more strongly supported or substantially softened.

OpenEval supports the scientific context and rationale claims (C3-C4, C19-C21, C27-C28, C31, C128-C129) as well-supported by literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/context claims.

Peer reviewers raised significant concerns about patch tension calibration and physiological relevance (C59-C60, C134), requesting acknowledgment of limitations. No corresponding OpenEval result specifically addresses these methodological concerns about tension measurements.
